prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: hit while turning left in Katy, Texas. Injury: neck strain. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1258; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not give my full name in the transcript. You can refer to me as the plaintiff.

Q: That's fine. Let's start with the accident. Where did it happen?

A: At an intersection in Katy, Texas. I was making a left turn across the opposite lanes at a signalized intersection.

Q: What were you doing right before the impact?

A: I had stopped at the light, then got the green arrow. I started into the turn slowly and was about halfway across when another vehicle came through from the other direction and struck the front passenger side of my car.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle before the collision?

A: Not clearly. I noticed headlights but I was focused on the oncoming traffic that had been clear when I started the turn.

Q: Did you feel anything right after the impact?

A: My head snapped forward and then back. My neck hurt almost immediately, and I felt stiff across the back of my shoulders.

Q: Did you seek medical attention that day?

A: Yes. I was taken by ambulance to a local emergency room. They checked me over, took some X-rays, and sent me home with a diagnosis of a neck strain and a prescription for a muscle relaxer.

Q: What treatment have you received since then?

A: I've been going to physical therapy about three times a week. I also saw my primary care doctor twice for follow-up visits. The therapy includes heat, gentle stretching, and exercises for my upper back and neck.

Q: How has your daily life been affected?

A: Quite a bit at first. I couldn't turn my head to check my blind spot, so I had my husband drive for the first few weeks. Sitting at my desk for more than an hour causes pain, so I've had to take breaks and stand up often. I also stopped my weekend hiking because carrying a backpack aggravates it.

Q: Are your symptoms improving?

A: Yes, gradually. The headaches have decreased and I can turn my head further than I could a month ago. Some stiffness still remains in the mornings, though.

Q: Have you had any prior neck or back problems?

A: No, nothing that required treatment before this accident.
